title: unify sdks: auth/retries, streaming ergonomics, parity fixes, version bumps
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Python 0.8.0 / TypeScript 1.4.0 / Go 0.6.2: unify auth/retries behavior; improved streaming ergonomics and parity across SDKs; bug fixes and performance tweaks.
description:
Context: We have had divergent auth and retry behaviors across SDKs which caused confusing developer ergonomics and a few production incidents where transient auth failures were retried incorrectly. This PR unifies the behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs: a shared retry policy (configurable backoff + idempotency hints), consistent auth refresh semantics (automatic refresh for short-lived credentials + explicit refresh hooks), and small ergonomics improvements for streaming APIs so behavior and examples match across languages.

What this changes: consolidated retry middleware and policy, new streaming helper utilities (context managers / async iterators parity), minor rework of auth token refresh paths to centralize refresh and add observability hooks, parity fixes where TS/Go previously differed from Python (headers, metadata propagation, cancelation behavior). Also bumps package versions and updates changelogs.

Motivation: reduce cross-SDK surprises for customers maintaining multi-language clients; make it easy to reason about retry bounds and streaming cancellation semantics; unblock Redwood examples and quickstarts that use mixed-language samples.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement shared retry policy across SDKs
- [x] Add idempotency hint support to retry decisions
- [x] Centralize short-lived auth refresh and expose refresh hook
- [x] Improve streaming ergonomics: Python context manager, TS async iterator, Go reader abstraction
- [x] Update examples and docs snippets (quickstarts)
- [x] Bump versions and changelogs
- [x] Add unit and integration tests for cross-language parity

Compatibility / migration notes: Default runtime behavior is backward-compatible. Projects that rely on custom retry middlewares should opt-in to the new shared middleware or pin to previous SDK minor versions. Streaming helper names are new but old primitives remain available for one release and are marked deprecated. See migration_notes.md in each SDK for mechanical changes.

Testing and validation: Unit test suites across all SDKs updated and passing; integration tests run against local test server for streaming cancelation semantics; manual smoke tests with sandbox keys. CI flakiness observed initially on TS streaming tests (race in cancel path) — fixed by small debounce in the client cancel path.

Related: ENG-5123 (cross-SDK ergonomics), ENG-5190 (retry policy standardization).

Priya Singh: Unit tests look good. One nit about function naming in Go streaming Reader - prefer 'Close' to 'Abort' for consistency with io.Closer. Updated to Close.
Liam Chen: Approve after tests are green.
